﴿The Bedouins say﴾, i.e., those spoken of at the beginning of the surah. ﴿"We have believed"﴾, i.e., in Allah and His Messenger, so we are believers, supposing that merely uttering the root of faith is the mark of every noble quality and goodness. ﴿Say, "You have not believed"﴾, i.e., you are not believers, even if you report it, because faith is speech and action. ﴿But say, "We have submitted"﴾, i.e., we have yielded and entered into peace, out of fear of captivity and killing. ﴿For faith has not yet entered your hearts﴾, i.e., for if faith had settled in the hearts, its effect would have appeared upon the body, and its truthfulness would have become manifest in righteous deeds and in keeping away from committing what is forbidden, for every truth has a reality and every claim has a witness.

If it is said: After His words ﴿Say, "You have not believed"﴾, does the phrase ﴿for faith has not yet entered your hearts﴾ appear to be a repetition without an independent new benefit? The answer: The benefit of His words ﴿You have not believed﴾ is the refutation of their claim, and His words ﴿for faith has not yet entered your hearts﴾ specify the time for what they were commanded to say, as if it were said to them: "But say, 'We have submitted,' while the agreement of your hearts with your tongues has not yet been established." For it is a statement standing in the place of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the pronoun in "say". The meaning of expectation in "lammā" indicates that these people will believe afterward, so there is no repetition. This is what al-Zamakhshari indicated, and he preferred that the sentence be a circumstantial clause rather than a new independent statement from Him, the Exalted, since the latter would not convey what has been mentioned.

Remarks:

First: In al-Iklil, it says: Whoever does not regard faith (īmān) and submission (islām) as synonymous has taken evidence from this verse, holding that between them there is general and specific relation in absolute terms, because submission is yielding to outward action, while faith is the heart's affirmation, as He said: ﴿for faith has not yet entered your hearts﴾. End of quote.

This argument is extremely weak, because their being synonymous in the sacred law does not prevent using each of them in its linguistic meaning in some contexts. Clarifying that is left to the contextual indicators, which are clear here. Otherwise, the verse ﴿Indeed, the religion with Allah is submission﴾ [Al-Imran: 19] is the strongest proclamation of their unity. Among the fine points is that what they said about the poor (faqīr) and the needy (miskīn) may be said of faith and submission: when they are combined they separate, and when they separate they combine. Faith, submission and similar terms are purely legal terms, and the Law has applied them only to speech and action, as the Imam Ibn Hazm clarified in al-Fasl, so consult it.

Second: In al-Iklil, it says: In the verse there is a refutation of the Karramiyya in their claim that faith is merely verbal affirmation without the heart's commitment, which is evident. Imam Ibn Hazm, among others, has fully refuted them in al-Fasl, so refer to it.

Third: It has been said: The apparent expectation would be that He says: "Say: Do not say, 'We have believed,' but say, 'We have submitted.'" Or: "You have not believed, but you have submitted." He turned away from this to this arrangement to avoid forbidding them to speak of faith and asserting their submission, since the condition for its validity in the Law is absent. It has also been said that it is ihtibak (a form of elliptical balancing), and its underlying form is: "You have not believed, so do not say, 'We have believed,' but you have submitted, so say, 'We have submitted,'" omitting from each part the counterpart of what was affirmed in the other. The first is more eloquent, because they claimed faith, so it was negated for them, then He corrected it, saying: "Abandon the claim of faith, and claim submission, for that is what should proceed from you in accordance with its reality." Thus He negated faith and affirmed for them the utterance of submission without attributing it to them, and this is more eloquent than the mentioned ihtibak, while also being free of omission without a clear indicator. This is what is found in al-Qadi and its glosses.

﴿And if you obey Allah and His Messenger﴾, i.e., by complying with their commands and refraining from what they forbid. The address is to these Bedouins who say "We have believed": ﴿He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds﴾, i.e., He will not wrong you in the rewards of your deeds in any way, nor will He diminish their reward for you.

Al-Zamakhshari said: It is said: "al-Sultan deprived him of his right with the utmost deprivation" (alatahu al-sultan haqqahu ashadda al-alt). This is the dialect of Ghatafan, and the dialect of Asad and the people of the Hijaz is "lātahu laytan." al-Asmai related from Umm Hisham al-Sulamiyya that she said: "Praise be to Allah, who is not overcome, nor deprived, nor is He silenced by voices." It was also read in both dialects: lā yiltakum and lā ya'iltakum. Similar in meaning is His word: ﴿So no soul will be wronged at all﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 47]. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, i.e., to whoever obeys Him and repents to Him from his past sins. So turn to Him, O Bedouins, and repent from hypocrisy, and firmly establish faith in your hearts along with acting upon its requirements, and He will forgive you and have mercy upon you.

Then the Exalted explained faith and what makes the believer a believer, with His words:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[15] ﴿The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, then did not doubt, and strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah. Those are the truthful.﴾

﴿The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, then did not doubt﴾ meaning: no doubt entered their souls concerning what they believed in, namely the oneness of Allah, the prophethood of His Prophet, and they obligated their souls to obey Allah and obey His Messenger, and to act upon what was obligatory for them of the duties of Allah, without any doubt about the obligation of that upon them. ﴿And strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah﴾ meaning: they struggled against the polytheists by spending their wealth and giving up their lives in fighting them, in accordance with what Allah commanded them of fighting them. That is His path, "so that the word of Allah is supreme, and the word of those who disbelieve is the lowest" (9:40). Ibn Jarir said: We have mentioned repeatedly that restricting "the path of Allah" to fighting the aggressive disbelievers is a case of restricting the general to its most important and highest individuals; otherwise, "the path of Allah" encompasses all acts of worship and obedience, because they are all in the way of His purpose.

Al-Shihab said: He mentioned wealth first because of people's eagerness for it, for a person's wealth is the sibling of his soul. And "strove" means: exerted effort. Or its object is implied, i.e., the enemy, or the self and desire.

﴿Those are the truthful﴾ meaning: those who were truthful in their claim of faith, as the effect of truthfulness appears upon their limbs and their deeds and words confirm it. In this there is an implicit rebuke that refutes those Bedouins in their claim of faith, and it conveys restriction (ḥaṣr). That is: they are the truthful, not those; or their faith is a faith of sincerity and earnestness.

Notes:

First: Al-Qasimi said in (al-Iklil): The verse is evidence that deeds are part of faith. We have already mentioned that this is something on which there is no disagreement among the early scholars (salaf), and one should refer to what Ibn Hazm, may Allah have mercy on him, expounded in (al-Fisal).

Second: Al-Qashani said: In His words, ﴿The believers are only﴾, the verse is an indication of genuine, valid faith, which is certainty firmly established in the heart, with which there is no doubt, not that which occurs in fleeting thoughts. The believers are thus the certain ones, whose firm quality of certainty overcame their hearts over their souls and illuminated them with its lights, so that the quality of the hearts became rooted in them until the limbs were affected by it, and it was not possible for them except to proceed according to its judgment and to be subjected to its state. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿and strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah﴾ after the negation of doubt from them, because spending wealth and life in the way of truth is the requirement of firm certainty and its effect outwardly. End.

Third: Al-Zamakhshari said in (al-Kashshaf): If you ask: what is the meaning of "then" (thumma) here, when it denotes sequence in time, while not doubting must be concurrent with faith, since it is a attribute within it, as you have explained, that faith conveys the meaning of trust and tranquility, whose reality is certainty, and the absence of doubt? I say: the answer follows two approaches:

The first: whoever has faith may be confronted by Satan, or some misleading people, after the expansion of the breast, so they cause him doubt and cast into his heart what diminishes his certainty; or he himself reflects in an unsound way by which he falls into doubt, and then persists in that, headstrong, not seeking a way out. So the true believers are described as distant from these destructive matters. A parallel to this is His words: ﴿Then they remained steadfast﴾ (46:13).

(p-5475) The second: since certainty and the removal of doubt are the essence of faith, they were singled out for mention after faith was mentioned, to draw attention to their place. And it was joined to faith by the particle of sequence, to indicate that it is settled through a long, extended period, fresh and renewed. End.

That is: either it is for the negation of doubt from them in what follows, indicating that just as they did not doubt at first, no doubt arose in them afterward; so the sequence is temporal, not in rank, as explained regarding His words ﴿Then they remained steadfast﴾ (46:13). Or he joined it to it by the conjunction of Gabriel to the angels, to indicate its originality in faith, until it is as if it were something else. Thus there is an indication of its continuity, both in the past and in the present.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[16] ﴿Say: "Will you inform Allah of your religion, when Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth? And Allah is Knowing of all things."﴾

﴿Say﴾ — i.e., to these Bedouins who say with their mouths, "We have believed": ﴿Will you inform Allah of your religion?﴾ — i.e., will you tell Him by your saying "We have believed" and by your obedience to Him, so that you may be among the believers in His sight, while you are not concerned with His knowledge of what you are upon? Here "ta'lim" (teaching, in the sense of informing and telling) is used, and therefore it takes the second object with the preposition bi (in). It has also been said that it takes bi because it is made to imply the sense of encompassing (ihata) or awareness (shu'ur). In this there is a rebuke to them and a reproach. That is: if their saying "We have believed" is an informing of the creatures, then there is no proof of its truthfulness; and if it is addressed to the Exalted Truth, then it has no meaning, for how could they inform Him when He is the Knower of all things? As He said: ﴿And Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾

Ibn Jarir said: This is what Allah had already conveyed to these Bedouins, forbidding them from lying and from saying other than what they hold in their religion. That is: Allah encompasses all things and knows them, so beware of saying the opposite of what He knows of your inner selves, lest His punishment befall you, for nothing is hidden from Him.

Then he pointed to another kind of their coarseness, concluded with a warning to them, by His saying, exalted is He:

(p-5476)

The Discourse on the Interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying:

[17] ﴿They consider it a favour to you that they have embraced Islam. Say: "Do not consider your Islam a favour to me. Rather, God confers a favour upon you that He has guided you to faith, if you are truthful."﴾

﴿They consider it a favour to you that they have embraced Islam﴾ meaning: they submitted and increased the number of your followers. ﴿Say: "Do not consider your Islam a favour to me"﴾ meaning: by your Islam, since there is no benefit from it returning to me: ﴿Whoever is guided, it is only for his own self﴾ [al-Isra': 15]. ﴿Rather, God confers a favour upon you that He has guided you to faith, if you are truthful﴾ meaning: in your saying "We have believed." But God knows from your hearts that you are liars, since He has knowledge of the unseen, as He said:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[18] ﴿Indeed, Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾

﴿Indeed, Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾ Ibn Jarir said: His mention, exalted is He, says: Indeed Allah, O Bedouins, nothing is hidden from Him: the truthful among you from the liar, and the one among you who enters the religion of Islam out of desire for it, and the one who enters it out of fear of the Messenger and his army. So do not teach us your religion, or the secrets of your hearts, for nothing in the hidden depths of the heavens and the earth is concealed from Him.

Remarks:

First: The Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The Banu Asad came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! We have embraced Islam, whereas the Arabs fought you, and we did not fight you.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Their understanding is little, and Satan speaks through their tongues.'" And this verse was revealed.

Ibn Zayd said: These verses were revealed concerning the Bedouins. It is not far-fetched that those spoken of at the end of the surah are among the coarse Bedouins, not those meant at its beginning, and they were grouped with them because of their shared harshness and roughness of speech. It is also possible that the report concerns one tribe, and Allah knows best.

Second: Regarding His saying: ﴿Rather, Allah confers favour upon you﴾ [al-Hujurat: 17] and so on, there is an observance of Allah's favour, the bounty lies in guidance, and there is the duty of giving thanks for it and acknowledging it, just as "the Prophet (ﷺ) said to the Ansar (Helpers) on the day of Hunayn: 'O assembly of the Ansar! Did I not find you astray, and Allah guided you through me? Were you not scattered, and Allah united you through me? Were you not in need, and Allah enriched you through me?' Whenever he said something, they would say: 'Allah and His Messenger are more gracious.'"

How subtle is the statement of Abu Ishaq al-Sabi in the preface of one of his books, after praising Allah, exalted is He: "He sent to them messengers from among them, guiding them to the straight path and the great triumph, and turning them away from the blameworthy way and the ill-fated destination. The last of them in time in this world, and the first of them in mention on the Day of Religion, the heaviest of them in the balance with Allah, the clearest of them in proof and evidence, the furthest of them in virtue to the utmost limit, and the most dazzling of them in miracle and sign: Muhammad (ﷺ), with abundant peace, whom He took as His chosen friend and beloved, and sent to His servants as a bringer of glad tidings and a warner, at a time when people had gone away with Satan, turned away from the Most Merciful, severed the ties of kinship, shed forbidden blood, committed crimes, and deemed sins lawful. Their noses were proud in acts of disobedience, and their souls were zealous in what was not for the sake of Allah. They called upon partners along with Him, ascribed equals to Him, and worshipped besides Him what neither hears nor sees and cannot avail them at all. He (ﷺ) never ceased to cast into their ears the virtues of faith, and to recite to their hearts the striking verses of the Qur'an, calling them to the worship of Allah with gentleness when he was alone, and with force when he found helpers and soldiers. He never saw a trace of disbelief without obliterating and erasing it, nor a mark without removing and effacing it, nor a deceptive proof without unveiling and refuting it, nor a raised pillar without bringing it down and laying it low, until he struck truth with its cheek, split it open with its structure, shone with its lamp, and gleamed with its brightness. Allah drew this community out of the lowest pit of the Fire and raised it to the summit of the righteous and the pious. Its rope was joined after it had been severed, its community was united after its dispersal, it gathered after division, and it made covenants after strife. So may Allah bless him with a pure and growing blessing, flowing and continuous, fulfilling his promise and raising his rank."

Third: Al-Razi said: This surah contains guidance for the believers to noble characteristics. These are either with Allah, exalted is He, or with the Messenger (ﷺ), or with others from among the human kind. And these are of two kinds: either they are upon the way of the believers and within the rank of obedience, or they are outside of it, and that is the wicked. And the one who enters their group and follows their way is either present with them or absent from them. Thus there are five categories:

The first: relates to the side of Allah.

The second: to the side of the Messenger.

The third: to the side of the wicked.

The fourth: to the present believer.

The fifth: to the absent believer.

Allah, exalted is He, mentioned in this surah five times: "O you who believe," and in each instance He guided to a noble trait in connection with one of the five categories.

He said first: ﴿O you who believe, do not put forward [anything] before Allah and His Messenger﴾ [al-Hujurat: 1]. The mention of the Messenger was to explain obedience to Allah, because it is not known except through the word of the Messenger of Allah.

He said second: ﴿O you who believe, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet﴾ [al-Hujurat: 2], to explain the obligation of respecting the Prophet (ﷺ).

He said third: ﴿O you who believe, if a wicked person comes to you with news﴾ [al-Hujurat: 6], to explain the obligation of guarding against relying on their words, for they intend to cause strife among you. He explained this when commenting on His saying: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight﴾ [al-Hujurat: 9].

He said fourth: ﴿O you who believe, let not a people ridicule another people﴾ [al-Hujurat: 11], and He said: ﴿And do not insult one another﴾ [al-Hujurat: 11], to explain the obligation of abandoning the harming of believers in their presence and belittling their condition and standing.

He said fifth: ﴿O you who believe, avoid much suspicion, for indeed some suspicion is sin﴾ [al-Hujurat: 12], and He said: ﴿And do not spy﴾ [al-Hujurat: 12], and He said: ﴿And do not backbite one another﴾ [al-Hujurat: 12], to explain the obligation of guarding against violating the honour of a believer in his absence, and He mentioned what would hurt him were he present. This is in the utmost excellence of arrangement.

If it is said: Why did He not mention the believer before the wicked, so that the ranks would be graded: beginning with Allah and His Messenger, then the present believer, then the absent believer, then the wicked?

We say: Allah placed first what is most important, so He mentioned the side of Allah, then the side of the Messenger, then He mentioned what leads to fighting among the groups of Muslims due to listening to the speech of the wicked and relying on it, for it mentions everything that is most repellent to hearts. As for the present or absent believer, they do not harm a believer to the point of leading to fighting. Do you not see that Allah, exalted is He, mentioned right after the report of the wicked person the verse of fighting, saying: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight﴾? End of quotation.
